trajectory.reasoning:
To determine if a triangle in 2D is a backface, we typically check the winding order of its vertices. In a standard right-handed coordinate system, if the vertices $a, b, c$ are ordered counter-clockwise, the face is considered front-facing. If they are ordered clockwise, it is a backface.

The winding order can be determined by calculating the 2D cross product (the z-component of the 3D cross product) of the vectors $(b - a)$ and $(c - a)$.
The formula for the 2D cross product is:
$\text{cross\_product} = (b.x - a.x) \times (c.y - a.y) - (b.y - a.y) \times (c.x - a.x)$

If the result is negative, the vertices are in clockwise order, indicating a backface.

action.code:
double val = (b.x - a.x) * (c.y - a.y) - (b.y - a.y) * (c.x - a.x);
    return val < 0;
